_about: The review questions, one packet per chapter key. The 96 approved on 2026-10-01/02 (the trimmed September packets), renumbered to the October 2026 chapters; the 11 rows the October text overtook reworded or dropped (operator 2026-10-08); the October update's full set is kept in spec-october-full.json. Keys starting with '_' are notes, not packets.

p2.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 2: Manual Mobility & General DME

**For:** Manual Mobility (Parth Dave, Manager)

rows.q: **Manual wheelchairs** — are the capacities, codes and coverage thresholds right? And when is the **Medline K3 Guardian 20"** billed as K0006 rather than K0003 with E2201?

rows.says: **Nebulizers:** new orders stay with Manual Mobility; refill supplies go to Resupply
**Upgrade fee waivers** — the table and diagram, including uncommon payers such as Workers' Compensation or the VA, which may pay the fee in full
**Texas-only coverage:** lift chairs through the Medicaid Waiver Program; shower chairs and tub benches through Texas Medicaid. The 3-in-1 commode can be covered by Medicare anywhere
**Walkers on an insurance order are never shipped out of state** — out of state is out of range (OOR). An **out-of-pocket** order lifts the state limit, but never the delivery radius

rows.q: **Other items** — knee walkers are out-of-pocket except through VGM Homelink, and blood pressure monitors are wrist-only. Are those right? And should **crutches (E0114)** be in the guide at all?
**Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 2's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p3.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 3: Respiratory & Resupply

**For:** Respiratory & Resupply (Nikunj Solanki, Manager)

rows.says: **Out-of-pocket purchases** are handled by the CSR team, who email intake, eligibility and Field Operations
**Nebulizer refill supplies** are handled by Resupply, at Medicare's allowances — and **no supply of any kind** ships more than a three-month quantity at once

**Resupply timing:** under Medicare the patient confirms within the 30 days before their supply runs out, and we ship no sooner than 10 days before. Texas Medicaid bills a month at a time, with eligibility checked before each shipment
**Quantity allowances** for trach, PAP and incontinence supplies
**Compliance requirements** — PAP usage and the follow-up visit, and the documentation for oxygen, ventilators and the low air loss mattress
**Ventilators:** after hours, dispatch the on-call RT immediately. If an MDO asks about a vent referral we can't find, check with the Respiratory & Resupply Manager first
**What we do and don't offer:** no new external or Purewick catheters, no new IPPB units; oximetry testing is available

**Your team's rows in the directory** — each resupply category (CPAP; incontinence and catheter; trach, suction and ventilator) has a named owner, backed up by the Respiratory & Resupply Manager; and the Respiratory Therapists row. Please check each holder, backup and contact

rows.q: **Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 3's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

**For:** Power — **Rajdeep Thakar** (Power Manager), **Erica Thongvan** (PAK) and **Ahmed Ramadan** (Qualifications)
**Also for:** **Ozaire (MD) Hawa** (Field Ops-Power) — questions marked **◆**

rows.q: **Qualifications documents** — is the list complete, and is each in the right group? Always: M.E. F2F, SWO, SE, LCMP Declaration, MRx. When applicable: Addendum, PT/OT Report Concurrence, PT Rx and Report, ATP Report

rows.says: **A Qualified Lead skips PAK but still gets a PPD**, from a Qualifications team member
**ATP evaluations** are scheduled by Field Ops-Power, up to 2–3 weeks out depending on the ATP's route. Virtual evaluations are scheduled only by Erica Thongvan ◆

**Medicare Advantage is primary**, not secondary

p6.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 6: Field Operations

**For:** Field Operations — **Parth Shah** (Manager) and **Mahesh Patel** (Supervisor)
**Also for:** **Ozaire (MD) Hawa** (Field Ops-Power) — questions marked **◆**

rows.says: **PMD pick-up requests:** adjustable problems and faults go to Service; affordability gets the EAA or a payment plan first; patient-owned chairs aren't picked up ◆
**Bed relocation:** generally not done; possible within the Dallas, San Antonio and Hawaii areas for rental beds, at $150. Either supervisor decides, and CSRs route the call to Service

**Shipping supplies:** no sooner than 10 days before the current supply runs out, and the ship date is the date of service. Overnight shipping is possible for respiratory supplies if the patient pays the difference
**Routing:** mask fitting goes to the Field Ops Q; freight companies go to Field Ops-Power with their name and delivery city; plus the common-call rules ◆

**Facility deliveries:** equipment no earlier than two days before discharge; the facility covers equipment during a Part A SNF stay; supplies only after discharge. **A PMD never goes to a hospital, rehab facility or SNF** — but it can go to a nursing home that is the patient's permanent residence, with the patient present ◆

rows.q: **Proof of delivery** — is the list of required contents right? And when are **delivery photos** taken, and when is a **driver's license** collected?
**Patient-responsibility balances** — when must *Pat. Resp.* be collected before delivery, and when can delivery be scheduled without it?

rows.says: **Used equipment:** a limited pool, mostly PWC K0821 and K0823 and CPAP; prescription items still need a prescription
**Backorders:** Field Ops updates the patient, and gives a date only if the manufacturer has
**The Purchase Capped Rental Form** is signed at delivery — CSRs check Artifacts for it before conceding a "nobody told me" call
**Upgrade fee returns:** unused, within 15 days, less a 20% restocking fee
**Oximetry:** delivery and pick-up are scheduled together

rows.q: **Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 6's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p7.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 7: Service

**For:** Service — **Arnav Pan** (Supervisor)

rows.says: **Who pays for a repair** — rental status and warranty decide, not time since delivery; and the categories where the usual rules don't apply (oxygen, frequent-and-substantial-servicing items, anything under warranty)

**A diagnostic visit carries a $75 out-of-pocket charge** when the patient refuses the requested photos or video of the equipment and the issue, or when one of our technicians recently found the equipment working and it is again fully functional; CSRs say so **before** booking. Is the fee $75, or $150? Are these the two conditions — or is it charged whenever no photos or video were sent? And is the visit free when the technician finds and repairs a fault?
**Loaners:** never offered unprompted; possible only while patient-owned equipment is repaired, and Service confirms
**PMD problems** come to Service — including discomfort and faults behind a pick-up request. Once a repair is arranged, the visit is scheduled through Field Ops-Power
**Warranties:** usually a year; Service requests coverage and the manufacturer decides; water damage commonly voids one
**Damaged, lost or stolen equipment:** irreparable damage means an accident or disaster, not neglect; lost or stolen needs a police report before a replacement request
**Ventilators:** the Trilogy is the only one we carry; issues go to the Service Q, and after hours the on-call RT is dispatched immediately
**Bed relocation:** either supervisor decides; if approved, Service tickets and validates it, and Field Ops schedules it
**Swap-outs:** with new documents needed, the CSR creates a pick-up ticket, notes it, and emails intake; otherwise Service creates a swap-out ticket
**Routing** — including wrong item versus expectation mismatch on resupply, and CPAP set-up

rows.q: **Chargers and batteries for non-customers** — does the caller's PMD have to be exactly a model we carry, or is a compatible charger or battery enough?

rows.says: **Turnaround** isn't quoted as a range — a few days for small issues, several weeks when a part comes from the manufacturer

rows.q: **Troubleshooting guides** — does your team have any, for power wheelchairs or other equipment? If so, please share them
**Resources** — any links to add to Chapter 7's resource list?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to your team?

p10.head:
# Review Packet — Chapter 10: Billing & Denials

**For:** Billing — **Bhoj Bhatt** (Billing Manager)

rows.says: **Hospice** covers equipment related to the terminal diagnosis; unrelated equipment can still be billed. Billing decides

rows.q: **Oxygen billing** — the conserver is included in the rental and coded **A9900**; accessories are included for all five years; UMS keeps ownership after 36 months. **Has UMS been billing the conserver as E1352?**

rows.says: **Rentals:** 13 paid months to ownership; a break over 60 days plus the rest of the rental month starts a new rental
**Resupply:** the 30-day contact and 10-day shipping windows; the ship date is the date of service
**Collecting payment:** out-of-pocket orders at the Item Master price, no sales tax unless flagged; Save Card only with permission
**Upgrade fee waivers** — rules A, B and C, uncommon payers, and checking Medicaid enrollment with Eligibility
**The EAA:** Billing processes it; usually 1–2 weeks; not available on out-of-pocket orders
**Medicaid and QMB:** QMB patients are never billed cost-sharing; Texas Medicaid as secondary can cover items Medicare never covers
**Deadlines:** timely filing — Medicare 12 months, Texas Medicaid 95 days; redeterminations within 120 days
**Cost estimates and billing scenarios**
**COB and ABNs:** only the patient can update COB; ABNs are Original Medicare only, signed before delivery
**What CSRs can and can't promise**

rows.q: **Resources** — Chapter 10 has no resource list. Are there documents, forms or links CSRs should have?
**Anything else?** Is anything missing, out of date, or worth changing — and what should a CSR have ready before transferring a call to Billing?
